The 2022 FIFA World Cup final was the final match of the 2022 FIFA World Cup, the 22nd edition of the FIFA competition for men's national football teams. The match was played at Lusail Stadium in Lusail, Qatar, on 18 December 2022, Qatar National Day, and was contested by Argentina and France.

Argentina took the lead in the 23rd minute when Lionel Messi converted a penalty after Angel Di Maria was tripped in the box by Ousmane Dembélé. Thirteen minutes later, Di Maria finished off a counter-attack to double Argentina's lead. France failed to register a single shot on goal in the first half and manager Didier Deschamps made two substitutions before the interval, bringing on Randal Kolo Muani and Marcus Thuram.

France leveled the match late in the second half through two goals by Kylian Mbappé within 97 seconds. The first was an 80th-minute penalty, awarded after Nicolas Otamendi brought down Kolo Muani, and the second was a volley from inside the penalty area 97 seconds later. The match went to extra time, where Messi scored his second goal in the 108th minute to give Argentina a 3-2 lead. However, Mbappé converted a second penalty in the 118th minute after his shot hit Gonzalo Montiel's arm, becoming the second player after Geoff Hurst to score a hat-trick in a World Cup final.

In the penalty shootout, Argentina won 4-2 after Kingsley Coman's penalty was saved by Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez and Aurelien Tchouaméni shot wide. Montiel scored the decisive fourth penalty for Argentina. Argentina won their third World Cup title, their first since 1986.
